info.title: Pocketmark HTTP API
info.description: Native API for your personal bookmark library. JSON errors have an error field. Browser requests use the existing owner session automatically; integrations send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Named keys cannot manage the account, API keys or full backups. First-run setup, login and health are public. Mutations enforce same-origin browser checks; configure POCKETMARK_ORIGIN to the exact public origin behind a reverse proxy. Limits measured in bytes are UTF-8 byte limits, not character counts. At most eight concurrent library requests; excess work returns 503. “Try it out” performs real operations on this instance. WebDAV /dav/ and removed Linkwarden compatibility routes are outside this reference. Public authentication has two separate slots and a five-second POST body deadline. /healthz has separate readiness slots; /livez checks process liveness independently. All HTTP requests except GET/HEAD health probes share a per-client token bucket: 10 requests/second, burst 100 by default (POCKETMARK_RATE_LIMIT and POCKETMARK_RATE_BURST). IPv6 clients share a /64. Rejection occurs before authentication/body reads and returns 429 with Retry-After. At most 256 sources are tracked; new sources fail closed at capacity. State resets on restart. Trusted forwarding requires POCKETMARK_TRUSTED_PROXIES. Security controls: owner-only actions, five-minute password confirmation, scoped expiring API keys, immediate key rotation and revocable browser sessions. WebDAV nonstandard methods are described by x-webdav-methods; they are not native OAS operations.

patch.summary: Rename, disable or reactivate an API key
patch.description: Owner only: a signed-in owner session is required. Named API keys receive 403. Disabling blocks subsequent API and WebDAV authentication; reactivation restores access with the same key. Revoked keys cannot be reactivated. Supply name, active, or both. Renaming preserves the credential, creation date and usage history and does not reactivate a disabled key. Owner session required; named keys are forbidden. Browser sessions require password confirmation within five minutes; otherwise 403 with code reauth_required, before any action. Use POST /api/reauth then retry.

post.description: Browser cookie required. Confirmation is session-bound, persists across restart and lasts five minutes. A successful login also counts as confirmation. Shares the bounded login rate limiter and serialized password work. Wrong password is 403; revoked/expired session is 401. Body limit: 4 KiB. Owner session required; named keys are forbidden.

get.description: At most 32 sessions, newest first. Omits expired and idle sessions. Contains no credentials or IP addresses. Legacy timestamps may be zero. Owner session required; named keys are forbidden.

patch.description: Browser cookie required. Allowed minutes: 15, 60, 1440, or 0 to disable inactivity expiry. Seven-day absolute expiry remains. New sessions default to 1440; legacy sessions retain absolute expiry only. Each authenticated HTTP request counts as activity, including background refresh. Body limit: 1 KiB. Owner session required; named keys are forbidden. Browser sessions require password confirmation within five minutes; otherwise 403 with code reauth_required, before any action. Use POST /api/reauth then retry.

delete.description: Requires a browser cookie; preserves its session. In-flight requests may finish. Owner session required; named keys are forbidden. post.description: Atomically invalidates the previous secret and returns a new one once. Preserves ID, name, permissions and expiry; resets last use. Disabled, expired or missing keys return 404.
